rules.statement: For children and descendants the legitima is two thirds of the estate, of which one third may be applied as mejora, leaving one third freely disposable. For ascendants it is one half, or one third where they concur with the spouse.

source.name: European e-Justice Portal, content supplied by the Spanish authorities

rules.notes: PARTIAL: arts. 806, 808 and 823 CC could not be read verbatim; BOE consolidated texts truncate long before Book III. Art. 807 (herederos forzosos) IS verified through a BOE-published DGSJFP resolution. Do not cite article numbers to customers until read.

rules.statement: The matrimonial property regime determines what falls into the estate; the legitima then determines how the estate is divided. Under sociedad de gananciales the community must be liquidated first, and only the deceased's half plus their private property forms the estate.
rules.notes: THE ERROR TO AVOID, and it is a common one. A tool that applies 'two thirds to the children' to the whole value of a jointly held Spanish property overstates the children's entitlement by roughly half. Keep the two calculations in separate, separately labelled steps.

rules.statement: Where the surviving spouse concurs with children or descendants they take the usufruct of the tercio de mejora. With only ascendants, the usufruct of one half. With neither, the usufruct of two thirds.

source.name: BOE consolidated text
source.ref: art. 834 CC, quoted verbatim in Resolucion DGSJFP

rules.notes: The third is the tercio de MEJORA, expressly. Not the legitima estricta and not the free third.

rules.statement: Under EU Regulation 650/2012 a person may choose the law of a State whose nationality they hold. The choice must be made expressly in a disposition of property upon death, or be demonstrated by its terms. Applies from 17 August 2015. The default is the law of habitual residence at death.

value.form: must appear in a will or equivalent testamentary instrument

rules.notes: THE SINGLE MOST USEFUL FACT FOR A FOREIGN OWNER. A Norwegian, Swedish, German, British or French owner can displace the Spanish legitima entirely, but ONLY through a will. The Regulation does not bind Denmark or Ireland and the UK never opted in, so a British national's choice of English law works from the Spanish side but is not symmetric. Art. 83 transitional rules for wills made before 17 August 2015 were NOT read.

rules.statement: Six autonomous communities have their own succession law that displaces the Civil Code: Aragon, Cataluna, Baleares, Navarra, Pais Vasco and Galicia.
rules.notes: The rules differ sharply, not marginally. Navarra and the Ayala valley in Alava have near-total freedom of testation; Catalonia's legitima is one quarter and is a credit rather than a share of assets. A tool covering the Costa Brava, Mallorca, Ibiza, the Basque Country or Galicia MUST branch here. Which foral law applies depends on the deceased's vecindad civil, not on where the property sits. This pushes any accurate heirship tool from Tier A to Tier B.

rules.statement: The state ISD scale runs from a bottom marginal rate of 7.65 percent on the first bracket to a top marginal rate of 34.00 percent on the excess above 797,555.08 euros.
rules.notes: CORRECTION: 36.5 percent is NOT the state top marginal rate. A top rate of 36.5 percent is widely quoted. Do not publish it. But 34 is not the ceiling on what is paid either: art. 22 multipliers by kinship group and pre-existing wealth run up to 2.4000 for Group IV, so an unmarried partner or non-relative faces an effective top rate well above 34. Most autonomous communities apply their own scale with very large reductions for spouses and children, so the state scale is the fallback, not the usual outcome.

rules.statement: Inheritance tax is due within six months of death, extendable by a further six months. Gift tax is due within thirty working days of the act.
rules.notes: PARTIAL on the extension: art. 68 is normally stated as requiring the request within the first FIVE months, but the text read said only 'before the original deadline expires'. Verify before coding. Gift tax is thirty WORKING days from the act itself, a much tighter window than the six months for inheritances and routinely missed. Late-filing surcharges follow late-filing.json, not the 5-percent-per-quarter schedule that still circulates.
